scope: Independent read-only language review of the four submitted complete mnc-Mong PR67 values. No candidate, application, repository or publication changes.
acceptance_definition: Accept means a complete value has adequate semantic and compositional grammatical support for integration at exactly the stated UTF-8 hash. It does not mean native idiom, historical UI attestation, runtime/layout certification or publication readiness. Hold means insufficient support for an identified full-value requirement, not necessarily a proven mistranslation.

entries.analysis: The complete phrase has position as the accusative object, tob seme as an adverbial precision modifier, and toktobure as the imperfect verbal noun/action label. The action-title expansion is appropriate to the coordinate control. The spatial precision evidence resolves the former person-oriented adjective concern. Determining a position does not intrinsically lock it against future changes. The final verbal noun is not treated as a complete imperative sentence.
primary_support: J, printed p.60, lower example (58): spatial tob seme; image independently viewed.
A, printed pp.197–198 / PDF pp.21–22: specifying numerical dimensions with toktobu-.
M, II.4 verbal forms and III syntax; E p.1 imperfect verbal nouns.
Q, tob/tob seme entries and toktobumbi entry 8-46a3.
entries.limits: This is a composed UI label. No source attests this exact complete title, and no native-speaker or modern UI terminology certification is claimed.

entries.source: The selected image is no longer in this assembly.
entries.target: ᠰᠣᠨᠵᠣᡥᠣ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡝᡵᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠠᠴᠠᠪᡠᠨ ᡳ ᡩᠣᡵᡤᡳ ᡩᡝ ᠪᡳᡥᡝ, ᡨᡝ ᠠᡴᡡ.
entries.independent_backtranslation: The selected image was inside this image combination; now it is absent there.
entries.analysis: Sonjoho qualifies the same selected image throughout. Ere identifies this assembly, whose genitive plus inside-locative is governed by past bihe. The short second clause retains the already established image and location while te contrasts now with the preceding past presence. This is a coherent way to express no longer here; it does not assert that the image file was deleted or ceased to exist globally. Nirugan acabun is an authored noun compound for an image combination/assemblage. Its intended collection sense is acceptable compositionally in this assembly UI, not on the strength of the historical app catalogue. The primary acabun entry alone concerns efficacy and must not be cited as if it directly attested an image assembly.
primary_support: M, bimbi/bihe paradigm, case marking, negation and head-final syntax.
G, printed pp.194–196: productive action/result nouns in -n including -bu-n, plus the nirugan derivation; pp.346–347 spatial genitive postpositions; pp.420–421 existence/copular forms.
Q, acabumbi combining senses at 6-13b2, 13-17a4 and 21-3b1; nirugan 7-37a1. These support composition, not an attested digital compound.
A, arithmetic composition with acabu- and inanimate absence constructions.
entries.secondary_support: L gives the union sense of acabun. It corroborates the compositional reading, with its mirror/transcription provenance limitation retained; it is not independent whole-sentence approval.
entries.limits: The elliptical second locative is contextual, not an explicit repetition. Idiomatic preference for the modern assembly compound remains untested. The old location-qualified akū oho sentence is not retrospectively adjudicated as meaning death, nor is its previous hold/approval status restored.
entries.independently_checked_reading: sonjoho nirugan ere nirugan acabun i dorgi de bihe, te akū.

entries.source: X and Y must be whole numbers from zero to 2147483647.
entries.target: 0, 1, 2, …, 2147483647 ᠰᡝᡵᡝ ᡨᠣᠨ ᡳ ᡩᠣᡵᡤᡳᠴᡳ X ᠵᠠᡳ Y ᠪᡝ ᠰᠣᠨᠵᠣ.
entries.independent_backtranslation: Choose X and Y from the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, 2147483647.
entries.analysis: The consecutive starting values, ellipsis and explicit final value define the closed nonnegative integer domain under ordinary modern numeric notation. Both 0 and 1 and the upper endpoint are present. The list is the complement of sere ton; its genitive plus dorgici supplies the selection domain. X jai Y is a coordinated object sharing accusative be, and sonjo is a directive. In a validation message, choosing coordinate values from this domain preserves the requirement in the English, without changing it to optional permission. The instruction does not require distinct X and Y values and does not itself specify a dropdown. The general noun ton need not be an independently coined technical term for integer because the enumeration restricts its domain.
primary_support: A, printed p.189 / PDF p.13: ordinary ton is explicitly distinguished from this manuscript’s special number category. Printed p.222 / PDF p.46 supplies a numeral-list + sere + ton construction.
F, printed p.244, entry 001398, independently visually inspected: selection from a genitive group with dorgici, accusative object and sonjo-.
M, II.1 case marking, II.4 stem imperative and III syntax; Q ordinary ton entry 7-38a1.
entries.limits: The ellipsis is modern mathematical notation, not a Qing convention established by these sources. Mixed-script display and accessibility reading remain untested. The earlier draft’s absent-value hold no longer describes this new complete value.

entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.
entries.target: ᡝᡵᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᡩᡝᡵᡤᡳ ᡥᠠᠰᡥᡡ ᡥᠣᡧᠣ ᠪᡝ ᡨᡠᠴᡳᠪᡠᡵᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᡩᡝ ᠰᡳᠨᡩᠠ. X ᠵᠠᡳ Y ᠪᡝ px ᡳ ᠪᠣᡩᠣᠮᡝ, 0, 1, 2, … ᠰᡝᡵᡝ ᡨᠣᠨ ᡳ ᡩᠣᡵᡤᡳᠴᡳ ᠰᠣᠨᠵᠣ. ᡝᡵᡝ ᠪᠠᡳᡨᠠ ᡤᡡᠸᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᡨᡝ ᠪᡳᠰᡳᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᠪᡝ ᡥᠠᠯᠠᡵᠠᡴᡡ. ᡠᠪᠠ ᡩᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠪᡝ ᠵᡳᠪᠰᡳᠪᡠᠴᡳ ᠣᠮᠪᡳ. ᠠᠮᠠᡤᠠ ᡩᠣᠰᡳᠮᠪᡠᡥᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠪᡝ ᠨᡝᠨᡝᠮᡝ ᡩᠣᠰᡳᠮᠪᡠᡥᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᡩᡝᠯᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᠮᠪᡳ. ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᠰᡳᠨᡩᠠᡥᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠪᡝ ᡤᡝᠮᡠ ᠪᠠᡴᡨᠠᡵᠠ ᠵᠠᠯᡳᠨ ᠠᠮᠪᠠ ᠣᠮᠪᡳ. ᡝᡵᡝ ᠪᠠᡳᡨᠠ ᡤᡳᡵᡳᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᠵᠠᡳ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᠠᠮᠪᠠ ᠠᠵᡳᡤᡝ ᠪᡝ ᡥᠠᠯᠠᡵᠠᡴᡡ.
entries.independent_backtranslation: Set this image’s upper-left corner on the output image’s drawing area. Using pixels as the unit, choose X and Y from 0, 1, 2, … . This operation leaves the other images’ current positions unchanged. Images may overlap here. Images brought in later are drawn over earlier ones. The drawing area becomes large to contain all placed images [the argument structure of this purpose clause remains insufficiently verified]. This operation leaves the trimming regions and image sizes unchanged.
entries.analysis: The full seven-clause value was read as one paragraph against every English clause. There is no omitted source sentence and no discovered reversal of coordinates, import order or the unchanged-image claims. However, H6 explicitly places nirugan be under bare baktara with the canvas as container-subject. The cited contextual Gorelova p.505 example has baktam-bu-ha, not this bare form, while the Qing index gives a capacity gloss and other retrieved contextual bare-verb examples admit fit/be accommodated readings. The broad contain/encompass gloss on G p.330 and in the secondary lexicon is positive lexical evidence but does not by itself settle this exact valency. This is a narrow evidence hold, not a proof that transitive baktambi is impossible. The complete Help must not be integrated until this clause is substantiated or a revised complete paragraph is reviewed.
primary_support: Q, physical corner/left/top, placing/drawing, overlap, temporal order and trimming lexemes.
M, case/participle/converb/negative grammar; G, genitive postpositions and purpose jalin.
A and F for the numeric-domain selection construction; E p.3 for permission through -ci ombi.
G p.505 was checked directly: its containment example includes -bu and cannot be silently equated with the submitted bare form.
entries.limits: No partial-clause acceptance is an integration approval for the paragraph. Girire ba and nirure ba are descriptive technical extensions with moderate confidence, not historical digital terms. Native idiom, runtime shaping and layout remain unverified.
entries.independently_checked_reading: ere nirugan i dergi hashū hošo be tucibure nirugan i nirure ba de sinda. X jai Y be px i bodome, 0, 1, 2, … sere ton i dorgici sonjo. ere baita gūwa nirugan i te bisire ba be halarakū. uba de nirugan be jibsibuci ombi. amaga dosimbuha nirugan be neneme dosimbuha nirugan i dele nirumbi. nirure ba sindaha nirugan be gemu baktara jalin amba ombi. ere baita girire ba jai nirugan i amba ajige be halarakū.

clauses.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas.
clauses.target: ᡝᡵᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᡩᡝᡵᡤᡳ ᡥᠠᠰᡥᡡ ᡥᠣᡧᠣ ᠪᡝ ᡨᡠᠴᡳᠪᡠᡵᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᡩᡝ ᠰᡳᠨᡩᠠ.
clauses.reading: ere nirugan i dergi hashū hošo be tucibure nirugan i nirure ba de sinda.
clauses.independent_analysis: The genitive ere nirugan identifies this same image. Dergi hashū modifies the physical corner, which is the accusative object of set; the output drawing area is locative. No logical-start or layer-top interpretation is substituted. The descriptive output-image phrase is somewhat long but interpretable.

clauses.source: X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero.
clauses.target: X ᠵᠠᡳ Y ᠪᡝ px ᡳ ᠪᠣᡩᠣᠮᡝ, 0, 1, 2, … ᠰᡝᡵᡝ ᡨᠣᠨ ᡳ ᡩᠣᡵᡤᡳᠴᡳ ᠰᠣᠨᠵᠣ.
clauses.reading: X jai Y be px i bodome, 0, 1, 2, … sere ton i dorgici sonjo.
clauses.independent_analysis: The shared X/Y object is calculated in the px unit and selected from consecutive counts beginning at 0. It excludes negative and fractional pixel values under modern enumeration notation. No maximum is added to this Help clause because the English itself has none.

clauses.source: Other images keep their current positions.
clauses.target: ᡝᡵᡝ ᠪᠠᡳᡨᠠ ᡤᡡᠸᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᡨᡝ ᠪᡳᠰᡳᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᠪᡝ ᡥᠠᠯᠠᡵᠠᡴᡡ.
clauses.reading: ere baita gūwa nirugan i te bisire ba be halarakū.
clauses.independent_analysis: The explicit operation subject and negative change predicate preserve the current positions of other images. The current-existence relative phrase belongs to those images’ places. This does not forbid later independent edits.

clauses.target: ᡠᠪᠠ ᡩᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠪᡝ ᠵᡳᠪᠰᡳᠪᡠᠴᡳ ᠣᠮᠪᡳ.
clauses.reading: uba de nirugan be jibsibuci ombi.
clauses.independent_analysis: The layering/overlap verb takes images as its object and -ci ombi provides permission. This is permission for overlap, not a requirement to overlap or a claim of partial transparency.

clauses.source: images imported later are drawn on top.
clauses.target: ᠠᠮᠠᡤᠠ ᡩᠣᠰᡳᠮᠪᡠᡥᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠪᡝ ᠨᡝᠨᡝᠮᡝ ᡩᠣᠰᡳᠮᠪᡠᡥᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᡩᡝᠯᡝ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᠮᠪᡳ.
clauses.reading: amaga dosimbuha nirugan be neneme dosimbuha nirugan i dele nirumbi.
clauses.independent_analysis: Later is attached to the import description, and the earlier-imported images are the genitive complement of dele. The latter construction expresses draw order over other images rather than motion toward the upper canvas edge. Modern import/render senses are contextual extensions. Exact collocation is not directly attested.

clauses.source: The canvas expands to include all placed images.
clauses.target: ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᠰᡳᠨᡩᠠᡥᠠ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᠪᡝ ᡤᡝᠮᡠ ᠪᠠᡴᡨᠠᡵᠠ ᠵᠠᠯᡳᠨ ᠠᠮᠪᠠ ᠣᠮᠪᡳ.
clauses.reading: nirure ba sindaha nirugan be gemu baktara jalin amba ombi.
clauses.independent_analysis: The main subject is the drawing area, so no image-scaling claim is made. Gemu scopes over all the images; placed images and purpose are explicit. Jalin after the uninflected participle is supported. Amba ombi is a contextual enlargement reading, but the accusative object governed by bare baktara is the outstanding issue. G p.505 illustrates the -bu form instead.

clauses.target: ᡝᡵᡝ ᠪᠠᡳᡨᠠ ᡤᡳᡵᡳᡵᡝ ᠪᠠ ᠵᠠᡳ ᠨᡳᡵᡠᡤᠠᠨ ᡳ ᠠᠮᠪᠠ ᠠᠵᡳᡤᡝ ᠪᡝ ᡥᠠᠯᠠᡵᠠᡴᡡ.
clauses.reading: ere baita girire ba jai nirugan i amba ajige be halarakū.
clauses.independent_analysis: The operation subject and shared final accusative/negative predicate preserve both coordinated objects. The genitive image phrase explicitly scopes size to images, avoiding a contradiction with canvas enlargement. Girire ba denotes a trimming area in this image-editing context; the source vocabulary does not independently specify a digital retained rectangle. Because the claim is that cropping is not changed, no new retained-versus-discarded-area operation is introduced.

unchanged_xy: Earlier X/Y acceptance is retained at its prior exact hashes. This report does not reapprove or alter those values.
important_corrections: The local Euclidean restriction on ton in one arithmetic manuscript is not a general lexical restriction. The ordinary number noun plus explicit domain is independently acceptable.

An animate mourning idiom cannot determine the meaning of every location-qualified inanimate akū oho sentence. This review assesses the new explicit past-presence/current-absence candidate and makes no death claim about the former candidate.
The candidate’s G p.505 containment citation uses a different morphological form from H6 and therefore does not, by itself, close H6 valency.

A newly found Tohoku primary-index search result (Toh-Asi-Ken-2010-37.pdf, [6-42b:2]) may supply positive transitive lexical evidence. Its indexed snippet is only a lead until the document is retrieved and inspected; it is not counted as a confirmed finding in this report.

script_and_bytes.method: Independently decoded every Manchu character to a conventional Latin reading for comparison with the supplied manual readings; did not generate or modify target translations by transliteration.
script_and_bytes.hash_method: SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 value bytes, no trailing newline

sources.title: Hitoshi Kuribayashi, Manchu index to the Qing trilingual dictionary
sources.kind: Scholarly index of primary Qing lexical material
sources.independent_use_and_limits: Primary lexical index inspected by searchable text and several direct page images. Broadly corroborates physical directions, place, image, draw, set, overlap and trimming vocabulary. Its acabun entry is efficacy, not a direct attestation of image assembly. Its bakta entry is lexical capacity evidence, not the requested object construction.

sources.title: P. G. von Möllendorff, A Manchu Grammar (1892)
sources.kind: Primary historical grammar and analysed native-script dialogue
sources.independent_use_and_limits: Primary historical grammar read through Wikisource. Supports modifier/head order, cases, stem directives, participles and negatives. Does not directly attest the modern UI sentences.

sources.title: Liliya M. Gorelova, Manchu Grammar (Brill, 2002)
sources.kind: Author-authored linguistic research with primary examples; retrieved scan is a third-party mirror
sources.independent_use_and_limits: Relevant pages independently read: 194–196 noun formation, 223 collective gemu, 326–330 adverbs, 346–347 spatial postpositions, 363 purpose jalin, 420–421 predicates, and 505 containment example. The p.505 verb includes -bu; it is not direct proof of the H6 bare-verb syntax. The hosted file is a third-party scan of the original research.
